svg.text: A tiny operating system: three tasks, one CPU, a context switch every 600 cycles
programs/22_multitasking.s on the cycle-exact model: 138 timer interrupts, 82,959 cycles, 17.9% of them in the kernel. make test checks it on the RTL too.
Who is running (the instruction retiring in WRITEBACK), cycle by cycle
Task control blocks: everything a task needs to continue later
round robin: the next pointers form a ring; mscratch holds the running task's block
mtime >= mtimecmp: the DECODE instruction is replaced, trap to mtvec (4 cycles)
swap: t6 = this task's block, the task's t6 is parked in mscratch
sd x1 .. x30, then t6, mepc
32 stores into the block: the task is now frozen in memory
follow the next pointer, skip tasks that are done
the new task's block and where it continues
31 loads: the new task's registers are back
jump to mepc, MIE on again: the other task runs as if never stopped
About 108 cycles per switch on average (14,835 kernel cycles / 138 switches):
the price of sharing the CPU. Real kernels also switch page tables and flush or tag the TLB.
